# BregSurv

> R package for **transfer learning in time-to-event analysis** through one objective: the target log-likelihood plus an integration weight `eta` times a Bregman divergence between the target model and an external one, `Q_eta(theta) = -loglik(theta) + eta * B_G(theta)`. The form of the external release fixes the divergence; the target may be a stratified Cox model (with tied times), a nested case–control design, or a discrete-time model, with a linear or neural-network risk score and an optional ridge / lasso / elastic-net penalty; `eta` is chosen by cross-validation on the target data.

- **Homepage**: https://um-kevinhe.github.io/BregSurv/
- **Install**: not yet on CRAN; `remotes::install_github("UM-KevinHe/BregSurv")`
- **Language**: R (user API) + C++ via RcppArmadillo (internal optimizer)
- **Maintainer**: Yubo Shao (ybshao@umich.edu)

---

## Start here: the interface (one call per analysis)

Every analysis makes three decisions, and the package has one object for each. Prefer this interface; the per-family functions below are the estimators it calls.

```r
fit <- cv.bregsurv(target, release, member = NULL, penalty = "none", etas = NULL, seed = 20260818)
```

**1. The target** — the model the user fits to their own data:

| user's data | constructor |
|---|---|
| follow-up time + event, full cohort | `target_cox(time, event, z, stratum = NULL, ties = c("none","breslow","exact"))` |
| matched case–control / nested case–control | `target_ncc(case, set, z)` (each matched set has exactly one case) |
| follow-up recorded in intervals 1..K | `target_discrete(interval, event, z, stratum = NULL, link = c("cloglog","logit"))` |
| any of the first and third, with a neural network | add `score = nn_score(hidden = c(128,128,128,128), dropout = 0.1)` (needs the `torch` package) |

**2. The release** — what the external source published:

| user's external information | constructor | members it supports |
|---|---|---|
| individual-level records (covariates with the target's column names + outcomes) | `release_records(z, time, event, stratum)`; matched: `release_records(z, case =, set =)`; discrete: `release_records(z, interval =, event =)` | `"composite"`; on a Cox target also `"mahalanobis"` and `"kl"` (through a Cox fit on the records) |
| coefficients, optionally with their precision matrix `Q` (inverse covariance / information) | `release_coef(beta, Q = NULL)` | `"mahalanobis"` and `"kl"` (KL not on a discrete target) |
| a risk score evaluated on the target subjects | `release_score(score)` | `"kl"` (Cox and matched targets) |
| coefficients + baseline cumulative-hazard increments over the target's K intervals, or an n x K matrix of interval hazards (absolute risk) | `release_model(beta, baseline)` / `release_model(hazard = H)` | `"kl"` on a discrete target; on Cox targets like `release_coef` |

**3. The member** — fixes the Bregman generator: `"composite"` (records → composite likelihood), `"mahalanobis"` (coefficients → Mahalanobis distance; Euclidean on the covered coordinates when `Q = NULL`), `"kl"` (model or risk score → Kullback–Leibler divergence), or omit the release for the target alone (`member = "none"`, `eta = 0`). `member = NULL` picks the first member the release supports. A neural target supports `"kl"` only.

**Penalty**: `penalty = "ridge" | "lasso" | "enet"` (with `alpha`) for linear targets; `eta` and `lambda` are chosen together, with a lambda path per eta. Not available on the matched composite member with ridge (no estimator), nor on neural targets.

**Comparing members.** With the same `seed` (fixed by default), every member fitted to the same target is scored on the same partition by the same criterion, so `fit$value` compares directly (lower is better): V&VH partial-likelihood loss for Cox (linear and neural), conditional-likelihood loss for matched designs, pooled held-out negative log-likelihood per subject for discrete targets. The external model used unchanged on a Cox target: `vvh_loss_fixed(z, delta, time, beta = beta_ext, folds = fit$folds)`.

```r
library(BregSurv)
data(ExampleData_lowdim); tr <- ExampleData_lowdim$train
tg <- target_cox(tr$time, tr$status, tr$z)
rl <- release_coef(ExampleData_lowdim$beta_external_fair)
fits <- list(kl = cv.bregsurv(tg, rl, member = "kl"),
             euclidean = cv.bregsurv(tg, rl, member = "mahalanobis"),
             kl_lasso = cv.bregsurv(tg, rl, member = "kl", penalty = "lasso"),
             target_only = cv.bregsurv(tg))
sapply(fits, `[[`, "value")        # one partition, one criterion
coef(fits$kl); fits$kl$eta; fits$kl$engine
predict(fits$kl, newz = ExampleData_lowdim$test$z, type = "survival", times = c(1, 2))
```

Result fields: `eta`, `lambda`, `value`, `criterion`, `coefficients` (linear targets), `folds`, `seed`, `path` (the CV table), `engine` (the estimator used), `fit` (its full result). `bregsurv(target, release, member, eta = , lambda = )` fits at a fixed weight without CV (not for neural targets).

On Cox and matched targets `cv.bregsurv()` calls the estimators below and returns exactly their result. Discrete-time targets use a built-in Fisher-scoring / proximal-Newton solver; neural targets use `torch`.

---

## The estimators behind the interface (call them directly for every option)

### Cox proportional hazards (full cohort)

| External mode | Low-dim fit | Ridge | Elastic net / LASSO | CV tuning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Individual-level | `cox_indi` | — | `cox_indi_enet` | `cv.cox_indi`, `cv.cox_indi_enet` |
| KL divergence | `coxkl` | `coxkl_ridge` | `coxkl_enet` | `cv.coxkl`, `cv.coxkl_ridge`, `cv.coxkl_enet` |
| KL divergence, tied event times | `coxkl_ties` | — | — | `cv.coxkl_ties` |
| Mahalanobis | `cox_MDTL` | `cox_MDTL_ridge` | `cox_MDTL_enet` | `cv.cox_MDTL`, `cv.cox_MDTL_ridge`, `cv.cox_MDTL_enet` |

### Nested case–control

| External mode | Low-dim fit | Ridge | Elastic net / LASSO | CV tuning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Individual-level | `ncc_indi` | — | `ncc_indi_enet` | `cv.ncc_indi`, `cv.ncc_indi_enet` |
| KL divergence | `ncckl` | — | `ncckl_enet` | `cv.ncckl`, `cv.ncckl_enet` |
| Mahalanobis | `ncc_MDTL` | — | `ncc_MDTL_enet` | `cv.ncc_MDTL`, `cv.ncc_MDTL_enet` |

NCC does **not** need tied-event-time handling (`coxkl_ties`-style) because in a standard NCC each matched set has exactly one event by construction. `ncckl` takes a `method = c("breslow", "exact")` argument for 1:m vs n:m matching semantics, but this is a likelihood form, not tie handling.

### Tuning, aggregation, and diagnostics (apply across families)

- `generate_eta(method = "exponential", n = 50, max_eta = ...)` — build an `eta` grid
- `bopt.coxkl(...)` — **Bayesian optimization** of `eta` for `coxkl` (faster than grid search when each evaluation is expensive)
- `cv.plot(cvfit)` — plot cross-validated performance curve vs `eta`
- `variable_importance(...)` — bootstrap selection frequency for high-dim KL/elastic-net fits
- `coxkl_enet.StabSelect(...)` / `cox_MDTL_enet.StabSelect(...)` — **stability selection** across subsamples (use when variable selection needs to be reproducible, not just predictive)
- `coxkl_enet_bagging(...)` / `cox_MDTL_enet_bagging(...)` — **bagged** integrated elastic net for variance reduction
- `coxkl_enet.multi(...)` — integrate **multiple external sources** (list of `beta_ext`) in one fit
- `test_eval`, `test_eval_ncc` — evaluate a fitted model on held-out test data
- `predict_surv_prob`, `get_baseline_hazard` — standard post-fit utilities

### S3 methods

Most fit objects have `plot()` methods; CV objects have companion `cv.plot()` calls. Stability selection objects plot selection-frequency paths. Variable importance objects plot top-k variable bar charts.

---

## Key parameters, uniform across functions

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `z` | Covariate matrix for **internal** data (n × p) |
| `delta` | Event indicator for internal data (1 = event, 0 = censored). **NCC functions use `y` instead.** |
| `time` | Observed times for internal data. **Not used in NCC functions.** |
| `stratum` | Stratum / matched-set ID. For Cox: optional (default = single stratum). For NCC: required — defines the matched sets. |
| `beta` | External coefficient vector: length `p`, or a **named** subset of `colnames(z)` (missing covariates auto zero-padded). Drives KL and Mahalanobis. |
| `RS` | Pre-computed external risk score `= Z %*% beta_ext`. Alternative to `beta` in `coxkl` / `coxkl_ties`. |
| `Q` | External p×p **precision / information** matrix (curvature of the external objective; must be symmetric positive-semidefinite) for Mahalanobis mode. May be named (matched to `colnames(z)`). `NULL` → (masked) identity. |
| `etas` | Vector of integration weights (grid). `eta = 0` recovers internal-only fit. |
| `eta` | Single integration weight (for penalized variants where `eta` is fixed while `lambda` is tuned). |
| `lambda` | Regularization strength for `_ridge` / `_enet`. Auto-generated path if omitted. |
| `alpha` | Elastic-net mix for `_enet`: `0` = ridge, `1` = LASSO, `(0,1)` = elastic net. |
| `nfolds` | CV folds (default 5). |
| `cv.criteria` | Performance criterion used by every `cv.*` function. See **CV criteria** section below. |
| `criteria` | Performance criterion used by non-CV helpers (`test_eval`, `test_eval_ncc`, `plot.*`, `bopt.coxkl`). Same spelling; different parameter from `cv.criteria`. |

### `eta` intuition

- `eta = 0` → pure internal Cox / NCC, no borrowing.
- Larger `eta` pulls the internal estimate further toward the external `beta`. The relationship is **monotonic in `eta`**: every increase in `eta` increases the influence of the external information, with no plateau or reversal.
- As `eta → ∞`, estimates converge to the external solution itself (the internal data effectively stops contributing).
- The **CV-optimal `eta` is usually a moderate value** — that is where the bias–variance trade-off is best: small enough that internal data still informs the fit, large enough to gain variance reduction from the external information.
- There is **no universal "correct" range**. Depends on data and compatibility between internal and external populations. Start with `generate_eta(method = "exponential", n = 50, max_eta = 10)` and inspect the CV curve; extend `max_eta` if the optimum sits near the upper boundary.

### `coxkl_ties` — handling tied event times

Use `coxkl_ties(..., ties = "breslow")` as the drop-in replacement for `coxkl` whenever your data has tied event times. **Always specify the `ties` argument explicitly in any example call** — the package does not auto-detect tie density, and the choice of approximation materially affects results. The two valid values are `"breslow"` (default, fast) and `"exact"` (slow, unbiased); there is **no Efron option** on `coxkl_ties`. A `comb_max = 1e7` safety cap stops the `"exact"` path from running indefinitely on heavy ties.

Why this matters: plain `coxkl` does **not** handle ties at all. It processes events as if all times were unique, which biases the partial likelihood whenever multiple events share an event time. With non-trivial tie density (≥5–10% of events tied), the bias is non-negligible and you should switch.

Detail on each `ties` option (the argument is **`ties`**, **not** `method=` — that name belongs to `ncckl`):

- `ties = "breslow"` (**default**) — Breslow's approximation. Fast, scales linearly. Recommended for most clinical / epidemiological data even at moderate-to-heavy tie density; bias is small in practice.
- `ties = "exact"` — exact partial likelihood. Enumerates all combinations within each tied risk set. Cost grows **combinatorially** with the per-time tie multiplicity, so it can become prohibitive for heavily tied large risk sets. Use only when ties are very heavy *and* runtime is acceptable.
- `comb_max = 1e7` — safety cap on the number of combinations evaluated under `ties = "exact"`. If a risk set would exceed this, the call errors out rather than running indefinitely. Raise this only if you genuinely need to handle a very large tied risk set and have verified the runtime.

**Note: `coxkl_ties` does not currently have `_ridge` or `_enet` companions.** Ties + regularization is not supported in this package. If you need both, you must choose: either accept the biased plain-Cox tie handling and use `coxkl_enet` / `coxkl_ridge`, or use `coxkl_ties` without regularization.

Minimal example call (always include `ties` explicitly):

```r
fit <- coxkl_ties(
  z = train$z, delta = train$status, time = train$time,
  stratum = train$stratum,
  beta  = beta_ext,
  etas  = generate_eta("exponential", n = 50, max_eta = 10),
  ties  = "breslow"     # or "exact" — must be specified
)
```

### CV criteria

Not all criteria apply to all functions.

- **Full-cohort Cox CV** (`cv.coxkl*`, `cv.cox_MDTL*`, `cv.cox_indi*`): `"V&VH"` (Verweij & Van Houwelingen, default), `"LinPred"` (linear-predictor loss), `"CIndex_pooled"`, `"CIndex_foldaverage"`.
- **NCC CV** (`cv.ncckl*`, `cv.ncc_indi*`, `cv.ncc_MDTL*`): `"loss"` (predicted deviance), `"AUC"`, `"CIndex"`, `"Brier"`.
- ⚠️ **The two families are disjoint and must not be mixed.** Do **not** pass an NCC criterion (`"AUC"` / `"Brier"` / `"loss"` / `"CIndex"`) to a Cox CV function, and do **not** pass a Cox criterion (`"V&VH"` / `"LinPred"` / `"CIndex_pooled"` / `"CIndex_foldaverage"`) to an NCC CV function. Cross-family misuse is **the most common API mistake** in this package: depending on the combination it may either error out or — worse — silently produce numbers with no statistical meaning. If unsure which family applies: full-cohort Cox data → Cox criteria; matched 1:m case–control data → NCC criteria.
- **Naming rule (consistent across the package).** Every function whose name starts with `cv.` uses the argument `cv.criteria`. Non-CV helpers (`test_eval`, `test_eval_ncc`, the `plot.*` S3 methods, and `bopt.coxkl`) use the shorter `criteria`. There are no exceptions.

---

## Worked examples (copy-ready)

### Example 1 — Low-dim Cox + external coefficients (KL divergence)

```r
library(BregSurv)
data(ExampleData_lowdim)

train <- ExampleData_lowdim$train
beta_ext <- ExampleData_lowdim$beta_external_fair

eta_list <- generate_eta(method = "exponential", n = 50, max_eta = 10)

# Fit over eta grid
fit <- coxkl(
  z       = train$z,
  delta   = train$status,
  time    = train$time,
  stratum = train$stratum,
  beta    = beta_ext,
  etas    = eta_list
)

# Tune eta via 5-fold CV with V&VH loss
cvfit <- cv.coxkl(
  z = train$z, delta = train$status, time = train$time,
  stratum = train$stratum, beta = beta_ext,
  etas = eta_list, nfolds = 5, cv.criteria = "V&VH", seed = 1
)
cv.plot(cvfit)
```

### Example 2 — Low-dim Cox + external coefficients + curvature (Mahalanobis)

```r
# Minimum input: beta; optionally supply A = Q (precision / information matrix).
# Q = NULL is valid and reduces the penalty to squared Euclidean.
fit <- cox_MDTL(
  z = train$z, delta = train$status, time = train$time,
  stratum = train$stratum,
  beta = beta_ext, Q = NULL,
  etas = eta_list
)
```

### Example 3 — Individual-level external data (composite likelihood)

```r
data(ExampleData_indi)

fit <- cox_indi(
  z_int = ExampleData_indi$internal$z,
  delta_int = ExampleData_indi$internal$status,
  time_int = ExampleData_indi$internal$time,
  stratum_int = ExampleData_indi$internal$stratum,
  z_ext = ExampleData_indi$external$z,
  delta_ext = ExampleData_indi$external$status,
  time_ext = ExampleData_indi$external$time,
  stratum_ext = ExampleData_indi$external$stratum,
  etas = generate_eta("exponential", n = 50, max_eta = 100)
)
```

### Example 4 — High-dim Cox + KL + LASSO, with CV

```r
data(ExampleData_highdim)
tr <- ExampleData_highdim$train

# Fixed eta, automatic lambda path
fit_lasso <- coxkl_enet(
  z = tr$z, delta = tr$status, time = tr$time, stratum = tr$stratum,
  beta = ExampleData_highdim$beta_external,
  eta = 1, alpha = 1    # alpha=1 ⇒ LASSO
)

# Tune eta by CV, internal lambda scan per eta
cvfit <- cv.coxkl_enet(
  z = tr$z, delta = tr$status, time = tr$time, stratum = tr$stratum,
  beta = ExampleData_highdim$beta_external,
  etas = generate_eta("exponential", n = 50, max_eta = 50),
  alpha = 1, nfolds = 5, cv.criteria = "V&VH", seed = 1
)
cv.plot(cvfit)
```

### Example 5 — NCC (matched case–control) + KL

```r
data(ExampleData_cc_lowdim)
tr <- ExampleData_cc_lowdim$train

fit <- ncckl(
  y       = tr$y,              # 0 = control, 1 = case
  z       = tr$z,
  stratum = tr$stratum,        # matched-set ID; REQUIRED
  etas    = generate_eta("exponential", n = 50, max_eta = 5),
  beta    = ExampleData_cc_lowdim$beta_external,
  method  = "breslow"          # or "exact"; identical for 1:M matching
)

cvfit <- cv.ncckl(
  y = tr$y, z = tr$z, stratum = tr$stratum,
  beta = ExampleData_cc_lowdim$beta_external,
  etas = generate_eta("exponential", n = 50, max_eta = 5),
  method = "exact", nfolds = 5, cv.criteria = "loss"
)
```

### Example 6 — Stability selection for reproducible variable selection

```r
# Use when you need a stable shortlist of important variables, not just prediction.
stab <- coxkl_enet.StabSelect(
  z = tr_hd$z, delta = tr_hd$status, time = tr_hd$time, stratum = tr_hd$stratum,
  beta = beta_ext_hd, etas = eta_grid,
  cv.criteria = "CIndex_pooled", B = 100, ncores = 10
)
plot(stab, threshold = 0.7)
```

### Example 7 — Bayesian optimization for `eta`

```r
opt <- bopt.coxkl(
  z = train$z, delta = train$status, time = train$time, stratum = train$stratum,
  beta = beta_ext,
  criteria = "V&VH",
  bounds_list = list(eta = c(0, 10)),
  n_iter = 20, seed = 1
)
opt$best_eta
```

---

## Returned-object conventions

Fit objects (e.g., `coxkl`, `cox_MDTL`, `ncckl`, and their `_ridge` / `_enet` variants) typically contain:

- `$eta` — sorted eta values used
- `$beta` — estimated coefficient **matrix** (p × n_eta, or p × n_lambda for penalized single-eta fits)
- `$linear.predictors` — n × (n_eta or n_lambda)
- `$likelihood` — log-partial-likelihood path
- `$data` — the (possibly reordered) input data used for fitting
- For `_enet` / `_ridge`: also `$lambda` (decreasing sequence)

CV objects contain fold-level performance tables plus an optimum summary (e.g., `$integrated_stat.best_per_eta` for `_enet` CVs).

Stability-selection objects return selection-frequency matrices along the penalty path.

Bagging objects return `$best_beta` (the aggregated coefficient vector, usable directly for prediction) and `$all_betas` (the bootstrap ensemble).

---

## Things an AI is likely to get wrong (read these)

1. **Do not use `coxkl` for matched case–control data.** Use `ncckl`. The sample-per-stratum structure is different.
2. **`ncckl` requires `stratum`.** Without it, the function assumes everyone is in one matched set — this is almost certainly not what the user wants.
3. **Do not pass `time` and `delta` to NCC functions.** NCC API uses `y` (binary case/control) and `stratum` (matched-set ID). The `time = 1, delta = y` mapping happens inside.
4. **`coxkl_ties` is only for full-cohort Cox with tied event times.** Do not suggest it for NCC. NCC functions have **no ties argument by construction** because each matched set contains exactly one event — tied event times are impossible by design. Do not invent a `ncckl_ties` function (it does not exist) and do not search for a ties option on `ncckl` / `ncc_indi` / `ncc_MDTL`. The `method = c("breslow", "exact")` argument that *does* appear on `ncckl` controls 1:m vs n:m matching likelihood form, not ties handling. See the dedicated `coxkl_ties` subsection above for the `ties` parameter (`"breslow"` / `"exact"`) and the `comb_max` safety cap; note also that `coxkl_ties` has no `_ridge` / `_enet` companion.
5. **`eta` and `lambda` are different things.** `eta` controls **external borrowing**. `lambda` controls **regularization** (only present in `_ridge` / `_enet`). Both can be tuned, but they play different roles.
6. **`alpha = 0` in `_enet` is ridge**, but the package provides a dedicated `_ridge` function that is preferred for pure-ridge use cases.
7. **For Mahalanobis without a curvature matrix**, pass `Q = NULL` (not `Q = diag(p)` — both work, but `NULL` is canonical).
8. **`cv.*` functions use `cv.criteria`; non-CV helpers use `criteria`.** This mirrors the function-name prefix: any `cv.*` function takes `cv.criteria = ...`. `test_eval`, `test_eval_ncc`, `plot.*`, and `bopt.coxkl` take `criteria = ...`. Do not mix them — passing the wrong name triggers `unused argument`.
9. **`generate_eta` does not auto-pick a sensible `max_eta`.** The user must choose based on the problem. If the CV optimum sits at the boundary, extend the grid and re-run.
10. **Stratified analysis is the default.** If `stratum` is omitted, the package silently assigns everyone to one stratum and fits a non-stratified model. This is fine for many problems but should be made explicit in output to users.

11. **Prefer `cv.bregsurv()` for new code.** It validates the release against the target, picks the estimator, passes `cv.criteria = "V&VH"` (Cox) or `"loss"` (matched) explicitly, and fixes the seed so members share a partition. `cv.coxkl_ties` alone defaults to `"CIndex_pooled"`.
12. **A discrete-time target cannot borrow from a coefficient vector through the KL member**: it needs interval hazards, i.e. `release_model(beta, baseline = dH0)` with the external Cox model's baseline cumulative-hazard increments over the same K intervals. A coefficient vector alone can enter a discrete target only through `"mahalanobis"`, and only with `link = "cloglog"`.
13. **Neural targets**: `penalty` must be `"none"`, the member must be `"kl"`, and `torch` must be installed (`install.packages("torch"); torch::install_torch()`). Fit them with `cv.bregsurv()`, not `bregsurv()`.

---

## Built-in example datasets

- `ExampleData_lowdim` — low-dim Cox: train (n=100), test (n=2000), 6 predictors, plus `beta_external_fair`
- `ExampleData_highdim` — high-dim Cox: train (n=200), test (n=2000), 50 predictors (6 signal + 44 AR(1) noise), plus `beta_external` and multi-source `beta_external.multi*`
- `ExampleData_indi` — paired internal/external individual-level Cox data (used for `cox_indi` examples)
- `ExampleData_cc_lowdim` — NCC: 200 matched sets (1:4) in train, 500 in test, 6 predictors, plus `beta_external` (used for `ncckl` / `ncc_MDTL` examples)
- `ExampleData_cc_highdim` — NCC high-dim: 50 matched sets (1:5) in train, 500 in test, 20 predictors, `beta_external`
- `ExampleData_cc_indi` — paired internal/external NCC data: internal 200 sets (1:4, n=1000), external 500 sets (1:4, n=2500), 6 predictors. Use for `ncc_indi` / `cv.ncc_indi` examples (the NCC analog of `ExampleData_indi`).
- Simulation helpers: `sim.cox.highdim`, `sim.binary`, `sim_integration`, `sim.matched_cc`

---

## Methodology references

The integrated objective functions have closed-form interpretations as **weighted pseudo-likelihoods**:

- **KL (Cox)**: `Q_eta(beta) = -loglik_internal(beta) + eta * D_KL(P_ext || P_int)` reduces to a weighted internal log-likelihood with a pseudo-event weight `(delta + eta * delta_tilde) / (1 + eta)` per subject, where `delta_tilde` is an externally-induced weight derived from `beta_ext`.
- **KL (NCC)**: analogous construction on matched sets; the pseudo-event weight is `(xi + eta * p_tilde) / (1 + eta)`.
- **Mahalanobis**: `Q_eta(beta) = -loglik_internal(beta) + (eta/2) (beta - beta_ext)' Q (beta - beta_ext)`. `Q` is the supplied precision matrix (or a masked identity if `NULL`).
- **KL (discrete time)**: the Bernoulli likelihood over person-intervals at risk with each outcome replaced by `(y_ik + eta * h_ext_ik) / (1 + eta)`, `h_ext` the external interval hazard (Wang et al., Annals of Applied Statistics 2025). The neural version trains a logistic-hazard network on the same soft targets.
- **Composite likelihood (individual-level)**: `loglik_int(beta) + eta * loglik_ext(beta)` — equivalent to stacking cohorts with observation weights `1` (internal) and `eta` (external), with strata kept separate so risk sets do not mix.

Full derivations are in the package vignettes (`vignette("coxkl")`, `vignette("ncc")`, `vignette("CV_Criteria")`, `vignette("BregSurv")`).
